## Analysis of the GSE161731 dataset

```{r}
library(tidyverse)

sample_meta <- read_tsv("data/_raw/RNA_sample_metadata.txt.gz", show_col_types = FALSE)
counts_df <- read.delim("data/_raw/RNA_count_matrix.txt.gz", check.names = FALSE) |>
  as_tibble(rownames = "gene_id")
```

## Clean Data

### Sample metadata

#### Selection of columns

Selection of the relevant columns for analysis.

```{r}
clean_sample_meta <- sample_meta |>
  select(-c("ips_received","ips_started","passage_received","media","passage_diff","diff_start","salmonella_date","atac_date","flow_date","medium_changes","terminated","open_access","ips_culture_days","passage_diff_bins","rna_extraction","rna_submit","library_pool","chemistry","rna_auto","status","ng_ul_mean","harvest_stimulation_days","macrophage_diff_days","EB_formation","macrophage_harvest","clone","line_id"))

clean_sample_meta |>
  slice_sample(n = 10)

```

#### Dealing with NAs

First, a check is made to see which columns have NAs, after the previous selection

```{r}
clean_sample_meta |>
  summarise(across(everything(), ~ sum(is.na(.))))
```

All missing values were identified in columns related to sample purity. Before deciding how to handle these missing values, we investigated whether their occurrence followed any pattern. For example, if missing values were associated with specific donors, experimental conditions or other sample characteristics.

```{r}
clean_sample_meta |> 
  filter(if_any(contains("purity"), is.na))
```

As we can see, there is a pattern: the NAs seemed to be grouped by the donor. However, there is some inconsistency, there are some donors, that have data in some purity columns, while others seem to have no data at all in every purity column. From this information, the decision was taken to only delete the rows related to the donors that have no data about the purity of their samples. This way, we make sure that further analysis is made on reliable data.

But first, we need to filter the donors that follow this characteristic, and then remove them.

```{r}
clean_sample_meta |> 
  group_by(donor) |> 
  select("donor",contains("purity")) |>
  filter(if_all(contains("purity"), is.na))
```

**///////DECIDE WHAT TO DO WITH THE REST OF NAs : put them in zero, have them, be the same value as the other columns, or maybe the columns "max_purity_filtered" and "mean_purity_filtered" , the ones that are NAs across all donors that have NAs in their samples, these columns maybe are not relevant and we can remove them//////**

```{r}
clean_sample_meta <- clean_sample_meta|>
  filter(!if_all(contains("purity"), is.na))
```

```{r}
#clean_sample_meta |>
  #filter(if_any(everything(), is.na))

#clean_sample_meta <- clean_sample_meta |>
  #drop_na()
```

#### Fixing columns naming

There are a couple of columns, with a odd name, specifically "SL1344", which refers to if it is a sample control or if the sample was infected with *Salmonella*; and also "IFNg", which refers if the sample was exposed to IFNγ (primed) or not (naive). Thus, the group decided to change this names for better understanding and consistency reasons.

```{r}
clean_sample_meta <- clean_sample_meta |>
  rename( SL1344_infection = SL1344,
    IFNg_status = IFNg)
```

#### Describing a cohort

///////Maybe take out the mean purity, all the values are the same//////

```{r}
library("table1")

clean_sample_meta |>
  mutate(
    condition_name    = factor(condition_name),
    sex               = factor(sex),
    rna_concentration = factor(rna_concentration),
    received_as       = factor(received_as)
  ) |>
  table1(
    x = formula(~ sex + received_as + rna_concentration + mean_purity | condition_name),
    data = _
  )
```

From this cohort, we can observe one more inconsistency, only one variable across all conditions has the column "received_as" with a value of "alive/frozen". Logically, this sample characteristic should belong to a sample from the same donor. Thus, an investigation for this hipothesis was conducted.

```{r}
clean_sample_meta |> 
  filter(received_as == "alive/frozen")

```

As we can see from the output, the samples from only one donor was received as alive/frozen. For consistency purposes, we decide to also remove the data from this donor.

```{r}
clean_sample_meta <- clean_sample_meta |>
 filter(!received_as == "alive/frozen")
```

### Counts data

For the counts data, genes with consistently low read counts were filtered out to reduce their influence on our analysis . Only genes with at least 10 counts in a minimum of 5 samples were retained. Subsequently, the dataset was transformed from wide to long format using `pivot_longer()`. This structure facilitates the integration of the count data with the sample metadata and supports subsequent exploratory analysis and visualisation.

//////should we do more than 5 samples tho? we have 336 samples, 5 seems very little//////

```{r}
counts_long <- counts_df |>
  # counts with at least 10 counts in at least 5 samples
  filter(rowSums(counts_df[-1] >= 10) >= 5) |> 
  pivot_longer(
    cols      = -gene_id,
    names_to  = "sample_id",
    values_to = "counts"
  )

counts_long 
```

### Creating one data set from two data sets

///// Text (bla bla bla) //////

```{r}
merged_data <- counts_long |>
  inner_join(clean_sample_meta, by = "sample_id")

merged_data |>
  distinct(sample_id, replicate) |>
  count(replicate)

merged_data
```

```{r}
gene_summary <- merged_data |>
  group_by(gene_id, condition_name) |>
  summarise(
    mean_counts = mean(counts),
    sd_counts   = sd(counts),
    .groups     = "drop"
  ) |>
  drop_na()

head(gene_summary)
```

```{r}
dim(gene_summary)

n_distinct(gene_summary$gene_id)
```
